QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_5

question.text: Konark Capital (Cat II) operates a WHOLE-FUND (European) waterfall. Called capital = INR 800 cr; total exit proceeds across all deals = INR 1,800 cr. 8% simple pref on called capital assumed for a 1-year holding, 100% catch-up, 80/20 split. What is the LP's TOTAL distribution?

explanation.text: The Logic: ROC: LP receives 800. Remaining = 1,000. Pref (8% on 800 for 1 yr) = 64 to LP. Remaining = 936. 100% catch-up: GP gets C such that C = 0.20*(64 + C) => C = 16. Remaining = 920. 80/20 split: LP 736, GP 184. LP total = 800 + 64 + 736 = INR 1,600 cr. GP total = 16 + 184 = 200. Sum = 1,800 — ties out. The Trap: INR 1,620 cr double-counts pref. INR 1,592 cr mis-applies catch-up to LP instead of GP. INR 1,560 cr uses 80/20 on the entire profit pool, ignoring the pref and catch-up tiers — common under a pure American deal-by-deal mental model. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C unique computational skill; XIX-A/B only test existence of pref and carry.
